justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Golf-specific movement assessment may improve return-to-sport outcomes; clinical rehab outcome data limited.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Online course plus in-person component; moderate cost; accessible to athletic trainers and PTs.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable only in golf performance, sports medicine with golf caseload, or sports PT with golf-playing patients.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: No insurance billing applicable; primarily cash-pay sports performance and golf fitness setting.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Limited employer demand; primarily cash-pay sports performance and golf fitness settings.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Golf clientele is affluent and routinely pays cash for performance work.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: TPI brand supports premium hourly rates ($150-250+) in golf markets.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Recognized brand, still uncommon enough to anchor a niche.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Other clinicians can be TPI-certified, but golfer relationships often follow the individual.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Strong direct-to-consumer recognition among golfers and golf pros.
justifications.business.efficiency: Level 1 is a weekend and ~$595; excellent ROI.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Commercial brand cert with no recognition for academic promotion.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Limited peer-reviewed output tied to TPI specifically.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Niche sports content rarely integrated into core DPT curriculum.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Golf biomechanics has literature but TPI screen evidence is thin.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Effectively never listed as preferred for faculty roles.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Short and cheap, but academically unproductive.
